name: Gabbai
overview: Gabbai was a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem. His identity is specifically noted in the biblical record as a Benjaminite residing in the city, highlighting his place within the post-exilic community. This situates him among those who were part of the restored population in Jerusalem.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Gabbai' means 'collector' and is a proper name mentioned in Nehemiah 11:8. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but its meaning may reflect a role or characteristic associated with the individual or his family.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Gabbai was a descendant of Benjamin. Beyond this tribal lineage, there are no additional family relationships documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Gabbai's significance lies in his identification as a Benjaminite living in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah, reflecting the repopulation and reestablishment of the city after the exile. His mention underscores the restoration of the tribes of Israel within Jerusalem and the continuity of the Benjaminite lineage. While not a prominent figure with a detailed narrative, his presence affirms the faithfulness of God's people returning to their land.
